results.evidence: Still only one South Buttress car-to-car gain figure: a 2024 trip report records 958 m (~3,143 ft), matching loss_ft. A 2018 West Ridge report from nearly the same pullout gives 5,000 to 8,050 ft (~3,050 ft) and the earlier-found West Ridge report 3,300 ft, but those are a different route. Guide and route pages (NCMG, Mountain Madness, climbing database page, a personal report) give no gain. Everything found says gain_ft 2500 is low, but no two sources state the same figure for this route. Would settle: a second South Buttress GPS track or guide stating the car-to-car gain.

A 2024 South Buttress report records 6.08 km (3.8 mi) round trip including the climb, which agrees with the itinerary's 3.8 mi and the summit pin's 2 mi; a 2018 West Ridge report from nearly the same pullout gives 3.6 mi round trip. dist_km is the one-way approach to the base, which ends in the boulder field below the summit, so a figure somewhat under 1.9 mi is expected; no source states the one-way approach distance to the gully, so it is not clear dist_km 2 is a different quantity. Would settle: a stated or GPS-measured pullout-to-gully distance.

results.fact: Parking location in access.notes (Rainy Pass trailhead lot vs SR 20 pullout)
results.correct_value: Roadside pullout on the north side of SR 20 about 1.5 mi west of Washington Pass
results.evidence: access.notes (rendered in ACCESS) says parking is a small lot at the Rainy Pass trailhead, while the approach, waypoints, road and approach_variants all start from the SR 20 pullout ~1.5 mi west of Washington Pass. The Mountaineers route page says to park along the highway near the Whistler Mountain sign about 3 mi east of Rainy Pass; a 2024 South Buttress trip report starts from a Highway 20 road pullout; a 2018 West Ridge report parks on Highway 20 about 0.5 mi west of the Blue Lake trailhead. All agree on a roadside pullout, not the Rainy Pass lot.

The beta's '5.7' is removed rather than replaced because the rock grade itself is unsettled (see discovered item).

results.evidence: The Umatilla NF day-use fee list and the Region 6 fee-site list both name only nine Umatilla fee sites (Elk Flats, Jubilee Lake, Meadow Creek, Panjab, Teepee, Three Forks, Timothy Springs, Tucannon, Twin Buttes); neither lists Middle Point or any FR 64 pullout, and the Middle Point Trailhead page states no fee. That supports the rendered 'no pass' fields, but both lists come from one publisher (the Forest Service); the climbing area page and the crag guide (unreachable) say nothing about passes. The disputed values live only in access._raw, which does not render. Would settle: an independent climbing or local source stating no pass is needed at the Dikes pullouts.
